A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCION research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original NanoGPT training experiments, Shakespeare language-model experiments, and CIFAR10 MLP/CNN evaluations, including hyperparameter-transfer and norm-control analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds ImageNet/DeiT results, longer GPT training comparisons and additional norm-choice evaluations.

M1.justification: The uSCG, SCG and ALMOND update templates remain unchanged. Section 3.1 and Table 6 extend the concrete SCION configurations from the existing sign-throughout alternative to ColNorm and RowNorm throughout the network, with appropriate layerwise scaling. The new Algorithm 3 mainly documents the existing layerwise framework.

E1.justification: v2 adds ImageNet-1k classification using DeiT-base, substantially broadening the vision evaluation beyond CIFAR10 MLPs/CNNs. FineWeb, Shakespeare and CIFAR10 coverage is retained; longer runs and additional norm configurations use existing coverage.

E2.justification: The existing Adam(W), Muon and Signum comparisons remain. v2's Table 10 caption additionally reports a CIFAR10 speedrun matching Muon with Frobenius normalization, a comparison not reported in v1's CNN evaluation; only a qualitative outcome is supplied. The new ImageNet experiment reuses AdamW, while newly discussed methods such as MARS are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The added DeiT protocol uses different normalization, activation, warmup, batch size and training budgets across optimizers: Table 11 specifies 300 epochs/batch 1024 for AdamW versus 200/batch 4096 for SCION variants. v2 also introduces a 20,000-step GPT comparison and a matched-loss timing procedure. Within retained CNN experiments, Table 10 switches reported output radii from 100/20 to 20/100 for unconstrained/constrained SCION; reruns are not established.

E4.justification: v2 adds RowNorm-throughout and ColNorm-throughout transfer sweeps (Figure 6), a long-run constrained-versus-unconstrained GPT comparison (Figure 9), and a corresponding DeiT norm-control comparison (Figure 12). Section 6 also adds matched-loss timing at batch size 6144. Existing input/output-norm sweeps, CNN momentum heatmaps and norm-growth analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 6 newly specifies three runs for the 124M SCION–Muon comparison; v1 does not disclose that repeat count for this comparison. This is newly reported run information, not evidence of an increase in runs. No new confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is described.

E6.justification: New outcomes include ImageNet accuracy curves targeting 81.8%, a reported 30% reduction in epochs and greater than 40% wallclock speedup under the new recipes, and 25% less wallclock time than Muon in the batch-6144 matched-loss experiment. Figures 6, 9 and 12 add further findings. Table 5's 3B losses remain 3.024, 2.909, 2.882 and 2.890; these are not improved same-setting scores.

T1.justification: The main convergence rates and most proofs remain. v2 explicitly restricts Lemma C.6 to alpha_k = 1, corrects Lemma D.1's squared Euclidean gradient norm to the dual norm, and corrects LMO signs and indexing in Tables 2–4. It also revises Lemma D.2 to assert (1 + 2/alpha)(1 - alpha) <= 1 - alpha/2, which is false, for example at alpha = 0.5.

C1.justification: The central claims about a unified LMO framework, convergence rates, hyperparameter transfer and memory efficiency persist. The introduction newly highlights stepsizes independent of the Lipschitz constant, explicitly describes Muon guarantees with and without weight decay, and expands the empirical contribution to ViT on ImageNet.

C2.justification: v2 adds possible explanations for large-batch benefits based on Euclidean noise analysis and rank-one gradients. It explicitly qualifies the width-transfer theory by alpha_k = 1, interprets new GPT/DeiT comparisons through norm control, and reports that RMSNorm benefits SCION without similarly benefiting AdamW. These refine the existing geometry and norm-control interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a SCION repository address, explicit layerwise pseudocode, activation specifications and ScaledReLU2 definition, input-layer radii, CNN batch-normalization handling, a learning-rate search grid, and detailed DeiT settings. These substantially expand reproducibility information without establishing changes to previously unspecified settings. The earlier Table 7 footnote explaining logit scaling for shared weights is removed.

R1.justification: Related-work positioning expands substantially through discussions of Moonlight, MARS/STORM, Lion-K, preconditioned SGD, and natural-gradient/TRPO methods. Additional references connect layerwise norms, normalized gradients and learning-rate schedules to prior work. These additions explain substantive relationships and distinctions beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The main section sequence, appendix organization and most prose are retained. Changes include focused explanatory additions, renaming 'Exclusively Sign' to 'Other norm choices,' adding the Scaled ReLU2 subsection and an Impact Statement, and updating affiliation/publication text and lemma/theorem terminology.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation is substantially reorganized: ImageNet replaces the main-text CIFAR10 plot, which moves into Figure 11; the sign-only comparison expands into four panels; Figure 9 gains a long-run panel; and a new DeiT comparison appears in Figure 12. Table 6 expands, Table 11 and Algorithm 3 are added, and several retained appendix plots are reordered or merged.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful additional empirical support through ImageNet, longer training and norm-choice analyses, alongside substantially better implementation disclosures and an explicit qualification of the width-transfer theorem. The gains are limited by the ImageNet comparison's simultaneous architecture and batch-size differences and by the invalid revised inequality in Lemma D.2. Overall, the empirical and reproducibility benefits support a modest net improvement.
